THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -9-  NC: 2023:KHC-K:1343  MFA No. 200816 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 200817 of 2018  MFA No. 201195 of 2018  MFA No. 201196 of 2018

JUDGMENT MFA No.200816/2018 and MFA No.200817/2018 are filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Aurad-B ( for short 'Tribunal') in MVC Nos.16/2016 and 17/2016, vide judgments and awards dated 09.02.2018.
2. MFA No.201195/2018 and MFA No.201196/2018 are filed by the insurer challenging the quantum of compensation awarded in the aforesaid two cases.

3. The claimants in both these appeals are the children of Sri.Peeranna @ Peeraji and Smt.Rukkamma @ Nagamma, who died in a road traffic accident on 08.09.2015, when they were crossing National Highway No.44 and were hit by a light goods vehicle bearing registration No.AP-20/TC-4187 (henceforth referred as - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1343 'offending vehicle').
The claimants contended that Peeranna was aged 47 years while Rukkamma was aged 38 years and both of them were selling donkey milk and clay pots and earning their livelihood.

The claimants claimed that their parents were earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- and Rs.6,000/- every month respectively and due to their untimely death in the accident, they were deprived of financial and emotional support.
Hence, they filed claim petitions claiming compensation.

4. The insurer denied the accident and claimed that the owner of the offending vehicle had allowed an unauthorized person to drive the offending vehicle as he did not possess a licence and therefore,
conditions of the insurance policy were violated and hence it was exonerated from liability.
5. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petitions were set down for trial.
The claimants were - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1343 examined as PWs.1 and 2, while a witness was examined as PW.3 and they marked Exs.P1 to P33.
The insurer did not lead any evidence.

6. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the driver of the offending vehicle was rash and negligent and was responsible for the accident which resulted in the death of Sri.Peeranna and Smt.Rukkamma.

The Tribunal held that deceased Sri.Peeranna was 46 years old at The Divisional Manager, National vs Balaji And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56537951/
8 the time of the accident while Smt.Rukkamma was aged 38 years old at the time of the accident.

 7.

The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation along with - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1343 interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petitions till the date of realization.

Being aggrieved by the quantum of The Divisional Manager, National vs Balaji And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56537951/
9 compensation, the claimants as well as the insurer are in appeal.

sentences.text: 8. The learned counsel for the appellants/claimants contended that the notional income of the deceased Sri.Peeranna ought to have been considered at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month and 25% of his notional income must have added for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency.

He contended that the Tribunal also failed to award adequate compensation under the conventional heads and therefore,
seeks enhancement.

Likewise, he contends that the income of the deceased Rukkamma be considered at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and loss of future prospects must have factored at 40% and enhanced compensation ought to have been awarded under the conventional heads.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurer contended that the postmortem report of Sri.Peeranna indicated his age as 62 years at the time of the death and the age of Smt.Rukkamma was 52 years at the time of her death.

The learned counsel contended that the Tribunal instead of considering the postmortem report, relied on certain documents such as, Adhar Card, voter identity card to consider the age of deceased Sri.Peeranna as 46 years and Smt.Rukkamma as 38 years.
She therefore contended that the compensation awarded be reduced by setting aside the impugned judgments and awards.
10. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants and learned counsel for the respondent/insurer.
I have also perused the records of the Tribunal and its judgments and awards.
11. The accident in question is not in dispute.
The death of Sri.Peeranna and Smt.Rukkamma in the accident - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1343 is also not in dispute.
The negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle is also not in dispute.
The documents placed on record such as, Adhar card and voter identity card of Sri.Peeranna and Smt.Rukkamma issued indicated their age as 46 and 38 years respectively.
These documents have been brought about long before the accident and based on the declaration of SriPeeranna and Smt.Rukkamma.
Therefore, the Tribunal was right in considering the documents placed on record to determine the age of Sri.Peeranna as 46 years and the age of Smt.Rukkamma as 38 years.
There is no error committed by the Tribunal in this regard.
12. In so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal must have considered the notional income at Rs.8,000/- per month.

In so far as deceased Sri.Peeranna is concerned, the Tribunal must have factored 25% of his notional income as loss of future prospects and must have The Divisional Manager, National vs Balaji And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56537951/
10 awarded just compensation.

Likewise, in the case of Smt.Rukkamma, the Tribunal must - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1343 have considered the notional income at Rs.8,000/- per month and 40%
ought to have been considered as loss of future prospects.

If the above exercise is conducted, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation which as follows:
In MFA No.200816/2018 (MVC No.16/2016) Loss of dependency Rs.11,70,000/-
(Rs.8,000+25%=10,000-2,500(1/4th) = Rs.7,500x12x13=11,70,000/-
Loss of parental consortium to claimant Rs.1,76,000/- Nos.2, 3, 4 and 5 at the rate of Rs.44,000/- each Funeral expenses and loss of estate Rs.33,000/-

Total Rs.13,79,000/-
In MFA No.200817/2018 (MVC No.17/2016) Loss of dependency Rs.15,12,000/-
(Rs.8,000+40%=11,200-2,800(1/4th) = Rs.8,400x12x15=15,12,000/-
Loss of consortium at the rate of Rs.2,20,000/- Rs.44,000/- each Funeral expenses and loss of estate Rs.33,000/-
Total Rs.17,65,000/-
 - 17 -  NC: 2023:KHC-K:1343 13.
In view of the above, the appeals filed by the claimants in MFA Nos.200816/2018 and 200817/2018 are allowed in part.
The appeals filed by the insurer in MFA Nos.201195/2018 and 201196/2018 are dismissed.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MVC No.16/2016 at a sum of Rs.8,54,800/- is enhanced to a sum of Rs.13,79,000 and the compensation awarded in MVC No.17/2016 in a sum of Rs.9,70,000/- is enhanced to a sum of Rs.17,65,000/- which are payable by the insurer along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of claim till realization.

The enhanced compensation of Rs.5,24,200/- in MFA No.200816/2018 and a sum of Rs.7,95,000/-
in MFA No.200817/2018 along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment and award.

opennyai_summary.facts:
3. The claimants in both these appeals are the children of Sri.Peeranna @ Peeraji and Smt.Rukkamma @ Nagamma, who died in a road traffic accident on 08.09.2015, when they were crossing National Highway No.44 and were hit by a light goods vehicle bearing registration No.AP-20/TC-4187 (henceforth referred as - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1343 'offending vehicle').
The claimants contended that Peeranna was aged 47 years while Rukkamma was aged 38 years and both of them were selling donkey milk and clay pots and earning their livelihood.
The claimants claimed that their parents were earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- and Rs.6,000/- every month respectively and due to their untimely death in the accident, they were deprived of financial and emotional support.
Hence, they filed claim petitions claiming compensation.
4. The insurer denied the accident and claimed that the owner of the offending vehicle had allowed an unauthorized person to drive the offending vehicle as he did not possess a licence and therefore,
conditions of the insurance policy were violated and hence it was exonerated from liability.
The insurer did not lead any evidence.
6. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the driver of the offending vehicle was rash and negligent and was responsible for the accident which resulted in the death of Sri.Peeranna and Smt.Rukkamma.
The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation along with - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1343 interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petitions till the date of realization.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
8. The learned counsel for the appellants/claimants contended that the notional income of the deceased Sri.Peeranna ought to have been considered at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month and 25% of his notional income must have added for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency.
He contended that the Tribunal also failed to award adequate compensation under the conventional heads and therefore,
seeks enhancement.
The learned counsel contended that the Tribunal instead of considering the postmortem report, relied on certain documents such as, Adhar Card, voter identity card to consider the age of deceased Sri.Peeranna as 46 years and Smt.Rukkamma as 38 years.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, the Tribunal was right in considering the documents placed on record to determine the age of Sri.Peeranna as 46 years and the age of Smt.Rukkamma as 38 years.
12. In so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal must have considered the notional income at Rs.8,000/- per month.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In so far as deceased Sri.Peeranna is concerned, the Tribunal must have factored 25% of his notional income as loss of future prospects and must have The Divisional Manager, National vs Balaji And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56537951/
10 awarded just compensation.
Likewise, in the case of Smt.Rukkamma, the Tribunal must - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1343 have considered the notional income at Rs.8,000/- per month and 40%
ought to have been considered as loss of future prospects.
If the above exercise is conducted, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation which as follows:
In MFA No.200816/2018 (MVC No.16/2016) Loss of dependency Rs.11,70,000/-
(Rs.8,000+25%=10,000-2,500(1/4th) = Rs.7,500x12x13=11,70,000/-
Loss of parental consortium to claimant Rs.1,76,000/- Nos.2, 3, 4 and 5 at the rate of Rs.44,000/- each Funeral expenses and loss of estate Rs.33,000/-
Total Rs.13,79,000/-
In MFA No.200817/2018 (MVC No.17/2016) Loss of dependency Rs.15,12,000/-
(Rs.8,000+40%=11,200-2,800(1/4th) = Rs.8,400x12x15=15,12,000/-
Loss of consortium at the rate of Rs.2,20,000/- Rs.44,000/- each Funeral expenses and loss of estate Rs.33,000/-
Total Rs.17,65,000/-
 - 17 -  NC: 2023:KHC-K:1343 13.
In view of the above, the appeals filed by the claimants in MFA Nos.200816/2018 and 200817/2018 are allowed in part.
The appeals filed by the insurer in MFA Nos.201195/2018 and 201196/2018 are dismissed.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MVC No.16/2016 at a sum of Rs.8,54,800/- is enhanced to a sum of Rs.13,79,000 and the compensation awarded in MVC No.17/2016 in a sum of Rs.9,70,000/- is enhanced to a sum of Rs.17,65,000/- which are payable by the insurer along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of claim till realization.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.5,24,200/- in MFA No.200816/2018 and a sum of Rs.7,95,000/-
in MFA No.200817/2018 along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment and award.
Out of the compensation and interest, 20% of the same shall be deposited in the name of claimant Nos.2, 3 and 4 in both the appeals in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years
Any amount deposited by the insurer is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
